description: Redis caching architecture — create common/caching/ module with CacheService, tenant-scoped key builders, TTL policies, stampede protection, and Redis failure fallback. Wire cache invalidation into model signals/viewset hooks using transaction.on_commit(). Cache menu catalog, branch config, user permissions, dashboard KPIs, reporting summaries, and inventory availability. Never cache payments/accounting balances as authoritative state. Independent of FEAT-001 (no dependency on its migration files).
steps: 1. Create backend/common/__init__.py and backend/common/apps.py (AppConfig name='common'). Add 'common' to LOCAL_APPS in backend/config/settings.py.
2. Create backend/common/caching/__init__.py (empty, re-exports CacheService for convenience).

3. Create backend/common/caching/policies.py. Define TTL constants as plain integers (seconds): MENU_CATALOG_TTL=300, BRANCH_CONFIG_TTL=600, USER_PERMISSIONS_TTL=300, DASHBOARD_KPI_TTL=120, REPORTING_SUMMARY_TTL=300, INVENTORY_AVAILABILITY_TTL=60. Define JITTER_FACTOR=0.15 (15% jitter applied as ±random). Define a helper function add_jitter(ttl: int) -> int that returns ttl + random.randint(-int(ttl*JITTER_FACTOR), int(ttl*JITTER_FACTOR)). Never cache: PAYMENTS_NO_CACHE=True, ACCOUNTING_NO_CACHE=True (sentinel constants documenting intent). Add docstring explaining each policy and why payments/accounting are excluded.

4. Create backend/common/caching/keys.py. Define key-builder functions that take authenticated server-side tenant IDs (never frontend-supplied). Functions: menu_catalog_key(branch_id, params_hash='') -> str returning 'rf:branch:{branch_id}:menu_catalog:{params_hash}'; branch_config_key(branch_id, key='') -> str returning 'rf:branch:{branch_id}:config:{key}'; user_permissions_key(user_id, branch_id='') -> str returning 'rf:user:{user_id}:perms:{branch_id}'; dashboard_kpi_key(user_id, restaurant_id='', branch_id='', date_str='') -> str returning 'rf:dashboard:{restaurant_id}:{branch_id}:{date_str}'; reporting_key(report_type, scope_hash, date_from, date_to) -> str returning 'rf:report:{report_type}:{scope_hash}:{date_from}:{date_to}'; inventory_availability_key(branch_id, item_id='') -> str returning 'rf:inv:{branch_id}:avail:{item_id}'. Add a make_params_hash(*args, **kwargs) helper that returns hashlib.md5(json.dumps(sorted list of args+kwargs, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]. All key functions must include explicit tenant-scope components — never a bare resource key.

5. Create backend/common/caching/services.py. Implement CacheService class with class methods only (no instance state). Methods: get(key) -> any|None — catches redis.exceptions.RedisError, logs warning, returns None on failure; set(key, value, ttl=300) — catches RedisError, logs warning, continues silently; delete(key) — catches RedisError, logs warning; delete_pattern(pattern) — iterates cache._cache.get_client().scan_iter(pattern) if available, else falls back to individual deletes — catches all exceptions; get_or_set(key, callable_fn, ttl=300, use_lock=False) — if use_lock=True, acquires a Redis lock via cache._cache.get_client().set(lock_key, '1', nx=True, ex=max(5, ttl//10)) before calling callable_fn; on lock failure returns callable_fn() directly (never blocks indefinitely); always catches RedisError and falls back to callable_fn(). For security-sensitive caches (permissions): get_secure(key) -> any|None — on RedisError returns CACHE_MISS_SENTINEL (a module-level sentinel object) so callers can distinguish 'not in cache' from 'Redis failed'; callers that see CACHE_MISS_SENTINEL must recheck DB. Import logging, use logger = logging.getLogger('common.caching').

6. Create backend/common/caching/invalidation.py. Define invalidation functions that use transaction.on_commit() so invalidation only fires after a successful DB commit. Functions: invalidate_menu_catalog(branch_id) — deletes rf:branch:{branch_id}:menu_catalog:* pattern; invalidate_branch_config(branch_id, key='') — deletes branch_config_key(branch_id, key) or the whole branch config pattern if key=''; invalidate_user_permissions(user_id, branch_id='') — if branch_id given deletes that specific key, else deletes rf:user:{user_id}:perms:*; invalidate_dashboard_kpis(restaurant_id='', branch_id='') — deletes matching dashboard KPI keys by pattern; invalidate_inventory_availability(branch_id, item_id='') — deletes matching inventory keys; invalidate_reporting_cache(report_type='', scope_hash='') — deletes matching reporting keys. Each function wraps its CacheService.delete/delete_pattern call in transaction.on_commit(lambda: ...) so it fires post-commit. Add a convenience register_menu_invalidation(sender, instance, **kwargs) signal handler that inspects the sender model name and calls the right invalidation function. Document in docstrings that these are best-effort: Redis failure must never cause a DB transaction to roll back.

7. Wire cache reads into backend/menu/views.py for the branch POS catalog endpoint (GET /api/menu/branches/<id>/catalog/). In the catalog view's get() method: build cache key using menu_catalog_key(branch_id, make_params_hash(**request.query_params)); try CacheService.get(key); on hit return cached response; on miss fetch queryset with existing select_related/prefetch_related, serialize, call CacheService.set(key, data, add_jitter(MENU_CATALOG_TTL)), return. Never cache if request has user-specific pricing overrides.

8. Wire cache reads into backend/reporting/services.py for dashboard KPIs. In get_dashboard_kpis (or the wrapper in reporting/services.py): build key using dashboard_kpi_key(user_id=str(user.pk), restaurant_id=str(restaurant_id or ''), branch_id=str(branch_id or ''), date_str=date.today().isoformat()); try CacheService.get(key); on miss call existing get_dashboard_kpis logic; set with add_jitter(DASHBOARD_KPI_TTL). The reporting/services.py already caches sales_trend using raw cache.get/set — migrate those calls to CacheService.get/set so Redis failures are handled uniformly. Use reporting_key() from keys.py for new cache keys in reporting services.

9. Wire cache reads for user permissions in backend/accounts/access.py (the has_permission / can_access_branch functions). Wrap permission lookups: build key using user_permissions_key(user_id, branch_id); call CacheService.get_secure(key); if result is CACHE_MISS_SENTINEL (Redis down), skip cache and query DB directly; if None (not cached), query DB, store result with add_jitter(USER_PERMISSIONS_TTL), return. This ensures Redis failure never silently grants or denies permissions.

10. Wire invalidation signals. In backend/menu/signals.py (create if not exists): connect post_save and post_delete signals for MenuItem, MenuItemPrice, MenuItemBranch to call transaction.on_commit(lambda: invalidate_menu_catalog(instance.branch_id)) where applicable. In backend/enterprise/signals.py (create if not exists): connect post_save for EnterpriseConfiguration to call transaction.on_commit(lambda: invalidate_branch_config(branch_id=...)). In backend/accounts/signals.py (create if not exists or add to existing): connect post_save for UserRoleAssignment to call transaction.on_commit(lambda: invalidate_user_permissions(user_id=instance.user_id)). Register signal handlers in each app's apps.py ready() method using the existing pattern in the codebase. For inventory: in backend/inventory/signals.py (create if not exists): connect post_save for StockBalance to call transaction.on_commit(lambda: invalidate_inventory_availability(branch_id=..., item_id=...)).

11. Create docs/caching_architecture.md at repo root. Document: cache key schema with examples; TTL table per data category; invalidation trigger table (which model save/delete triggers which cache invalidation); stampede protection via Redis lock in CacheService.get_or_set; Redis failure behavior per cache category (graceful fallback vs forced DB recheck for permissions); what is explicitly NOT cached (payments, accounting, audit logs) and why.
acceptance_criteria: backend/common/caching/ module exists with __init__.py, services.py, keys.py, invalidation.py, policies.py
'common' app added to INSTALLED_APPS in settings.py
CacheService.get() returns None (not raises) when Redis is unavailable
CacheService.get_secure() returns CACHE_MISS_SENTINEL (not None) when Redis is unavailable
Menu catalog cache key includes branch_id (tenant-scoped)
Dashboard KPI cache uses CacheService, not raw cache.get/set
User permissions cache uses get_secure with CACHE_MISS_SENTINEL fallback to DB
Signal handlers registered in apps.py ready() for menu, accounts, inventory, enterprise
python manage.py check returns zero errors
